user.title: Set up heating system
user.description: One system per Home Assistant: one house with one heat source. Add heating circuits and rooms afterwards as sub-entries.

data_description.name: Name of the system, e.g. “Vienna”. Shown on the “Heizung” page and in front of the entities.
data_description.manufacturer: How Heating Core talks to the heat source. Vaillant: setpoint to the zone via the myVaillant integration (cloud, write budget). Ökofen: operating mode heat/setback plus offset via the “Ökofen Pellematic Compact” integration; the Pellematic heating curve stays active. Set up the manufacturer integration first.

abort.already_configured: This heating system is already configured.

init.title: System settings

data.leitstand_expert: Expert log (full details of every run as notification)

init.description:
Applies to the whole system. Set comfort and setback per circuit or room on the “Heizung” page.

{hint}

data_description.min_trv_temp: Lower limit for all thermostats: frost protection, window open, summer.
data_description.budget_per_hour: How often per hour Heating Core may write to the boiler (cloud limit). Safety writes (window, emergency) don't count. Typical: 10–13.
data_description.away_entities: If any of these is on, the house is “Away” (e.g. input_boolean.global_away from geofencing). There is also the system's own Away switch.
data_description.guest_entity: Guests in the house: “Away” is ignored while this is on.
data_description.summer_entity: While on, heating rests: thermostats at minimum, boiler off (hot water keeps running), switched back on afterwards.
data_description.outdoor_sensor: Outdoor temperature for building compensation. Leave empty if unused.
data_description.weather_enabled: Raises the setpoint a little in cold weather, because walls and windows cool down. Not while away.
data_description.weather_zone3: Extra °C between 0 and +10 °C. No extra above.
data_description.boost_enabled: Faster heat-up: if a room is well below comfort, request more for a while. Better off with Ökofen – the heating curve sets the flow temperature itself, boost costs burner starts.
data_description.boost_threshold: Boost starts at this distance below comfort and ends when the room is nearly there.
data_description.humidity_enabled: Lowers the setpoint slightly at high humidity – humid air feels warmer. Needs a humidity sensor on the circuit.
data_description.humidity_drop: Drop in °C per 10 % humidity above 60 %, at most 2 °C.
data_description.push_enabled: Sends writes and new problems to phones. The problem notification in HA is always on.
data_description.notify_devices: Phones with the Home Assistant app that receive pushes.
data_description.quiet_schedule: While this schedule is on (e.g. at night), no pushes are sent.
data_description.leitstand_expert: After every run, all details (target, actual, decision, budget per circuit and room) as an HA notification. For troubleshooting.
data_description.room_demand_delta: A room raises the whole circuit only when it is this far below its comfort – otherwise it heats via its own thermostat and the slow boiler keeps running calmly. 0 = every room at once.
data_description.pre_heat_lead: Comfort starts this many hours before the schedule because the boiler is slow. The “Heizung” page then shows “Pre-heating for …”. 0 = schedule applies exactly.
data_description.summer_mean_sensor: Statistics helper with the rolling 72 h mean of the outdoor temperature. If set and the summer switch is an input_boolean, Heating Core switches summer itself – only while “Steuern” (control) is on. Empty = summer only by hand.
data_description.summer_limit: Summer from heating limit + 1.5 °C (72 h mean), heating season again below heating limit − 1.5 °C.
data_description.battery_min: Reports weak batteries of every device Heating Core uses (thermostats, sensors, window contacts), found automatically via their devices.
data_description.pressure_sensor: System pressure in bar. Leave empty if the system does not report it.
data_description.pressure_min: Below this an alarm “refill now”, up to 0.2 bar above a warning “refill soon”.
data_description.efficiency_sensor: E.g. COP/efficiency or a statistics helper with the 7-day mean. Only shown in the daily briefing.
data_description.briefing_time: Push with pressure, efficiency, reachability, pellets and open problems. Empty = no briefing. Paused in summer.
data_description.error_entity: E.g. binary_sensor.…_trouble_codes. Reports a fault right away via the problem notification and push.
data_description.device_health: Reports weak batteries and devices unreachable for more than 15 min – only devices Heating Core uses. Turn off if an automation of your own already does this for the whole home, otherwise every message arrives twice.

user.title: Heating circuit
user.description: A heating circuit is a branch with its own pump or setpoint at the heat source (e.g. radiators upstairs, floor heating).

data_description.name: Name of the circuit, e.g. “HC1 radiators upstairs”.
data_description.kind: Radiator or floor: circuit with a master thermostat at the heat source. Floor external: own pump and valves outside the heat source, released by boiler temperature.

reconfigure.title: Heating circuit
reconfigure.description: A heating circuit is a branch with its own pump or setpoint at the heat source (e.g. radiators upstairs, floor heating).

data_description.name: Name of the circuit, e.g. “HC1 radiators upstairs”.
data_description.kind: Radiator or floor: circuit with a master thermostat at the heat source. Floor external: own pump and valves outside the heat source, released by boiler temperature.

details.title: Heating circuit – devices
details.description:
Devices and demand sources of the circuit. Set comfort and setback afterwards on the “Heizung” page.

{hint}

data_description.master_climate: Zone or circuit at the heat source that Heating Core writes to.
data_description.presence_sensors: Presence sensors in the circuit's main room. Presence → comfort, even outside the schedule. Smoothing: “Heizung” page → “Grundwerte” → Presence.
data_description.schedule: Schedule helper: on = comfort, off = setback. Rooms without their own schedule follow it. Without schedule and presence the setback applies. Easiest to edit on the “Heizung” page.
data_description.window: Window contact in the main room. Open longer than “Window open after” → whole circuit to minimum.
data_description.temp_sensor: Room sensor in the main room. More accurate than the heat source's sensor; without it, that reading is used.
data_description.humidity_sensor: Humidity in the main room. Only used with humidity compensation (system settings).
data_description.pump_switch: Pump of this floor circuit. Runs only once valves are open and the boiler is warm enough.
data_description.source_temp_sensor: Boiler or buffer temperature that releases the floor circuit.
data_description.source_on: The floor pump may run above this boiler temperature.
data_description.source_off: Below this boiler temperature the pump is blocked. Must be below the release.
data_description.valve_delay_s: Wait this long after opening the valves before starting the pump.
data_description.hvac_mode: Zone mode after summer. Manual: setpoint directly. Time program (recommended): Heating Core sets and renews a quick veto – if HA fails, the boiler's own time program takes over again.
data_description.pre_heat_entity: Optional, e.g. for geofencing: while this switch is on, Heating Core pre-heats like the “Pre-heat” button and turns it off after the timeout or once presence/schedule takes over. Empty = only the built-in button.

user.title: Room
user.description: A room belongs to a heating circuit. The role says what is in the room; the matching fields follow in the next step.

data_description.name: Name of the room, e.g. “Office”. The same name in different circuits is fine.
data_description.circuit: The circuit the radiator or floor zone is connected to.
data_description.role: Own room: thermostat with its own control. Follows circuit: thermostat takes the circuit's setpoint. Floor zone: valve channels. Radiator without thermostat: display only in the diagram.

reconfigure.title: Room
reconfigure.description: A room belongs to a heating circuit. The role says what is in the room; the matching fields follow in the next step.

data_description.name: Name of the room, e.g. “Office”. The same name in different circuits is fine.
data_description.circuit: The circuit the radiator or floor zone is connected to.
data_description.role: Own room: thermostat with its own control. Follows circuit: thermostat takes the circuit's setpoint. Floor zone: valve channels. Radiator without thermostat: display only in the diagram.

details.title: Room – devices
details.description:
Devices of the room. Set comfort afterwards on the “Heizung” page; setback comes from the circuit.

{hint}

data_description.climate: The radiator thermostat (TRV) that receives the setpoint.
data_description.valves: Valve channels of this zone; they always switch together.
data_description.offset: Offset to the circuit setpoint, e.g. −2 °C for a cooler bedroom.
data_description.presence_sensors: Presence sensors in the room. Presence → comfort, even outside the schedule.
data_description.schedule: Own schedule for this room only. Empty = the circuit's schedule.
data_description.window: Window contact in the room. Open longer than “Window open after” → thermostat to minimum.
data_description.temp_sensor: Own room sensor – more accurate than the one inside the thermostat. Heating Core calibrates the thermostat with it.

room_sensor_blocks.title: {circuit}: Pellematic room sensor switches the circuit off

confirm.title: Change it on the Pellematic
confirm.description:
The Pellematic switched **{circuit}** off (“room temperature reached”) although rooms on this circuit still need heat. Its room sensor measures only one room and thereby blocks the whole circuit – the other rooms stay cold although their valves are open.

**How to change it** (only on the Pellematic display, in the Ökofen app or on my.oekofen.com, not in Home Assistant):
1. Open heating circuit **{circuit}**.
2. Set **room sensor off** or **room influence 0** (if the item is missing: installer level, code from your installer).
3. Keep **eco mode** of this circuit **off**.

Afterwards Heating Core controls the circuit via the rooms; the Pellematic heating curve stays active. Only confirm once it is changed – if the room sensor keeps blocking, this message comes back.
